When developing a website, developers often rely on CSS classes to style buttons, forms, navigation elements, and other interface components. This approach works well, but some situations require styles to depend on an element's HTML attributes rather than additional class names.

Industry observers note that CSS attribute selectors provide a practical solution. They allow developers to target elements based on whether an attribute exists, what value it contains, or whether its value matches a particular pattern. Used carefully, they can simplify styling and make reusable components easier to maintain.

Recent findings suggest that an attribute selector targets an HTML element using square brackets. For example, a developer can select every input field that has a required attribute:.

This rule applies to inputs with the required attribute, regardless of their input type.

Developers can also target a specific attribute value:.

This is useful when different input types need different visual treatments without introducing additional classes into the HTML.

Forms are a practical place to apply attribute selectors because HTML already provides attributes that describe how individual fields behave.

Sources indicate that consider a registration form containing email, password, and telephone fields. Each input can be styled according to its purpose:.

The CSS can target these fields independently:.

This approach keeps the markup descriptive while allowing the stylesheet to respond to the attributes already present in the document.

It has been revealed that one important distinction is that required indicates a validation requirement, while :invalid represents an input's current validity state. These should not be treated as interchangeable.

CSS provides several matching operators that help developers target more specific attribute values.

These operators can be useful when working with links, downloadable files, language attributes, and reusable components.

For example, a website might want to distinguish PDF downloads from ordinary navigation links:.

This adds a small visual indicator to links whose URLs end in .pdf.

Attribute selectors can also help identify links with different destinations or behaviors.

For example, external links that use HTTPS can receive a subtle visual indicator:.

However, matching an HTTPS URL does not necessarily prove that a link points to an external website. Internal links can also use HTTPS, so developers should consider the actual navigation requirements before applying special styling.

For more examples of selector combinations and matching rules, SitePoint's guide to CSS Attribute Selectors provides a useful reference.

Although attribute selectors are flexible, they should not replace every class-based styling decision.

A selector such as [class*="button"] can match unintended elements if their class names happen to contain the same text. Similarly, broad attribute rules may affect components that were not originally intended to receive those styles.

For predictable results, use exact attribute matching whenever possible and prefer descriptive classes for major component styling.

Developers should also remember that CSS selectors only control presentation. They do not replace JavaScript validation, server-side security checks, or proper HTML semantics.

The MDN documentation on attribute selectors provides further details about selector syntax, matching behavior, and supported operators.

Before adding attribute selectors to a large stylesheet, inspect the affected elements using browser developer tools.

A simple testing process includes:.

Check whether the selector matches the intended elements.

Test fields with different attribute values.

Verify disabled, required, and invalid form states.

Check navigation links and downloadable files.

Test the layout on mobile and desktop screens.

Review whether existing component styles are being unintentionally overridden.

This process helps identify unexpected matches before they affect the production interface.

CSS attribute selectors give developers another way to create flexible and maintainable interfaces without adding unnecessary classes to every HTML element.

Recent findings suggest that they are particularly useful for form styling, link identification, and components that already contain meaningful HTML attributes. By choosing precise selectors, understanding matching operators, and testing changes before deployment, developers can use this feature to write cleaner CSS while keeping their markup descriptive and organized.

It has been revealed that you need a YouTube API key the moment your app has to read anything from YouTube: a video's length, its view count, a channel's latest uploads. Getting one takes about five minutes. Using it well takes a little longer, because YouTube changed how its quota works in June 2026, and plenty of guides still describe the old rules.

In this guide we'll get a key, lock it down and test it. Then we'll use it from Node.js for three real jobs: adding up the length of a playlist, listing a channel's videos without spending a search, and estimating what a video earned. Along the way we'll cover what the YouTube API costs (nothing), how the 2026 quota works, and the errors you're most likely to hit.

It has been revealed that A YouTube API key identifies your project to the YouTube Data API v3. With just a key, you can read public data:.

A key isn't enough for anything that touches someone's account. Uploading videos, editing playlists or reading private data needs OAuth 2.0, where the user signs in and grants your app access.

Sources indicate that you'll need a Google account. The YouTube Data API is free, so there's nothing to pay for.

Sources indicate that the restrictions matter more than they look. A key is just a string in a URL, and anyone who copies an unrestricted one can spend your daily quota for you. With an API restriction, the key is useless for other Google APIs. With an application restriction, it only works from your server or your site. Changes to restrictions can take up to five minutes to apply, so don't panic if a request fails straight after you save.

Before writing any code, check the key with a single request. This one asks for the first video ever uploaded to YouTube, and uses the fields parameter to trim the response down to four values:.

Sources indicate that yes. There's no charge per request and no paid blueprint. Instead you get a daily quota, and since June 1, 2026 it's split into separate buckets:.

Google's quota calculator lists the cost of every method. Quotas reset at midnight Pacific Time. Every request costs at least 1 unit, including requests that fail, so a retry loop around a broken call can use up a day's quota on its own.

If you've read older guides, search is the big change. A search used to cost 100 units out of the same 10,000, so 100 searches emptied your whole day. Uploads were worse still, at about 1,600 units each until December 2025. Now both have their own buckets, and the 10,000 units are left for everything else.

YouTube first audits your project to check it follows the YouTube API Services Terms of Service, then someone from the API team gets back to you. Google doesn't give a timeline, so apply well before you need the extra quota.

According to recent reports, most projects never need to. The rest of this guide is about getting a lot done with very few units.

Industry observers note that A designer who once spent an afternoon searching stock libraries can now describe the picture they want and have four versions in under a minute. AI image generators have moved from curiosity to everyday tool for blog headers, product mockups, ad concepts, game art and slide decks. The quality gap between tools has narrowed, but the differences that remain matter a lot: how well each follows a detailed prompt, whether it can render readable text, how it handles edits, and what you are allowed to do with the result.

This guide compares six of the best-known options, what each does well and where each falls short. Models, plans and limits change often, so check each vendor's own pages before you commit to a workflow.

Sources indicate that openArt’s AI image generator puts several image models behind one interface. Its generator page lists models including GPT Image 2.5, Grok Imagine, Qwen Image 3, Nano Banana 2 and Seedream 5.0 Pro, and lets you create images from text prompts or reference photos. It also lists tools for camera angle control, upscaling, collages and a Character Builder for keeping characters consistent across scenes, with 4K export.

Best for: Creators who want to compare several models on the same prompt without juggling separate subscriptions and accounts.

Limitations: The page offers a free start but does not state credit amounts or initiative details, and it does not address commercial use, so check the pricing and licensing pages before using results for client work. Output quality depends on which model you pick.

Recent findings suggest that openAI's image generation in ChatGPT works inside the chat interface, which makes iteration natural: generate an image, then ask for changes in plain language. OpenAI highlights accurate text rendering, the ability to follow prompts with many distinct objects, and consistent characters across multi-turn edits. You can also upload reference images and have the model transform them. It handles both photorealistic and stylized looks.

Best for: Marketers and writers who want to describe, refine and re-describe an image without learning a latest tool.

Limitations: OpenAI notes that tall images such as posters can be cropped too tightly, and that dense small text, multilingual text and precise graphs can still go wrong. Images can take up to a minute to render. All generated images carry C2PA metadata identifying their source.

Gemini's image generation runs on Google's Nano Banana models. Google highlights character consistency, text rendering in many languages, combining several photos, precise editing and 2K resolution. A free tier covers image generation and editing, while the most advanced model requires a Google AI plan. You start from the "Create images" option in the Gemini app, then prompt or upload a picture to edit.

Best for: People who need to keep the same subject across several images, or who want to edit existing photos rapidly.

Sources indicate that limitations: Usage limits apply, and the strongest model is behind a paid plan. Images include an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible AI label, which is good for transparency but may not suit every use.

Recent findings suggest that midjourney is an independent research lab known for images with a strong, painterly look. Its official site points users to a sign-up flow and to a Discord community and help center for support. Many creators choose it for concept art, mood boards and illustration where style matters more than literal accuracy.

Best for: Artists, art directors and game designers who want rich, stylized results and enjoy exploring variations.

Limitations: I could not confirm current pricing, trial terms or feature details from Midjourney's public pages, so check them yourself before subscribing. The workflow can feel less like a normal app than the others on this list, and it is not the easiest route for precise, text-heavy graphics.

Adobe Firefly is built for professionals who already work in Creative Cloud. Adobe states that its Firefly models are commercially safe, trained on licensed Adobe Stock and public domain content, and outputs carry Content Credentials that show AI involvement. It offers text-to-image, image-to-image, sketch-to-image and style transfer, plus editing tools such as background removal, object removal, upscaling and generative expand. It connects with Photoshop, Illustrator, Lightroom and Adobe Express, and also lets you use partner models from other companies.

Best for: Designers and brand teams who need clear licensing and want AI inside the apps they already use.

Limitations: Intends work on a credit system, so heavy use adds up. Adobe lists a free tier with limited daily generations and paid plans starting at about $9.99 a month, but confirm current terms on its site.

Sources indicate that ideogram built its reputation on a problem that trips up many generators: readable text. Its current models are presented as producing clean typography in different layouts, with attention to prompt fidelity and reliable editing. It also offers an API with access to a catalog of models, and has released open weights for one earlier model for local use and customization under its license.

Best for: Posters, social graphics, logo concepts and anything where words are part of the image.

According to recent reports, limitations: The pages I checked did not describe a free plan, so look at current plans before relying on it. Like every generator, it still needs a human to proofread the text it produces.

According to recent reports, start with the job. If you want to compare several models side by side, try OpenArt. If you want to talk your way to a finished image, try ChatGPT or Gemini. If you need images that will sit inside a branded design workflow, Firefly is the safer fit. If you are chasing a distinctive look, Midjourney deserves a trial. If text must be perfect, test Ideogram.

Recent findings suggest that run the same prompt in two or three tools before paying. Differences in composition, hands, faces and text show up quickly, and they matter more than any feature list.

Reviews only go so far, because your own use case is what counts. Pick one realistic job, for example a 16:9 header image for a blog post about web performance, and run the same prompt through two or three tools. Write the prompt once and paste it unchanged, so the comparison is fair:.

Sources indicate that then score each result on five questions: Did it follow every instruction? Are there odd details in hands, edges or objects? Is any text spelled correctly? Does it still look good when cropped to a square? Could you license it for your project? Ten minutes of this teaches more than any feature list, and it shows how much editing each tool needs before you can publish.

Most readers of this guide will put these images on web pages, where a few habits matter more than the generator you choose.

There is no single best AI image generator. The right pick depends on whether you value conversation, style, licensing, control or typography. Test two or three on a real project, compare the output, and keep a human in charge of the final choice. Whatever you generate, review it for errors and label AI-made images clearly where your audience would expect it.

Recent findings suggest that are AI-generated images free to use commercially? It depends on the provider and your proposal. Read the licensing terms for the tool you use, and consider vendors that publish how their models were trained if you work for clients.

According to recent reports, which AI image generator is best for text in images? Ideogram and ChatGPT both highlight text rendering, and Gemini lists it as a feature. Test each with your own wording and proofread the result.

Do AI images have watermarks? Some do. OpenAI adds C2PA metadata, Google adds an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible label, and Adobe attaches Content Credentials.

Industry observers note that can I use more than one image model without separate accounts? Yes. Platforms such as OpenArt put several models in one interface, which makes side-by-side testing easier. Check the licensing terms for each model you use.

Sources indicate that should I add alt text to AI-generated images? Yes, when the image carries meaning. Describe what it highlights or why it is there. Purely decorative images can use an empty alt attribute, following the W3C guidance.

#11876. SEO For AI Crawlers: How to serve AI Agent friendly pages?

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (934 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sitepoint ↗ Open Full Page

SEO For AI Crawlers: How to serve AI Agent friendly pages?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • It has been revealed that AI-friendly pages are plain-text (usually markdown) versions of webpages that are meant for AI, rather than people.
  • Industry observers note that we ran this test at acme.bot on November 4, 2026, across 53 live pages on 43 host names.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

It has been revealed that AI-friendly pages are plain-text (usually markdown) versions of webpages that are meant for AI, rather than people. Websites typically determine that AI is requesting a page via the user agent, Accept header, or a specific .md URL.

Industry observers note that we ran this test at acme.bot on November 4, 2026, across 53 live pages on 43 host names. Because we targeted sites likely to do this, the sample leans towards developer tools.

While testing the HubSpot, Gymshark, Semrush and Profound web pages, we didn't find any markdown on the pages.

While it's a common practice in developer documentation, there's not much research or evidence that it helps AI visibility.

Dries Buytaert checked a month of Cloudflare logs and found no AI crawler using content negotiation. The crawlers reached his markdown only through dedicated URLs, by following an auto-discovery link. So a site that relies on Accept alone is serving coding agents - and, possibly, no crawlers at all.

Industry observers note that even when the request asks for HTML, Stripe's docs still send markdown to all six AI user agents we tested. They send HTML to Bingbot, Googlebot, and browsers. The Checkout page drops from 846 KB to 5.5 KB. Its markdown has links to other .md pages, keeping an agent in the text pages. The response to markdown comes with the header X-Robots-Tag: none to ensure it is kept out of search indexes. Sentry's docs route the same way.

Recent findings suggest that vercel pages (including the blog and pricing page) that we tried all returned markdown on request. Docs pages also go to AI user agents, unless the request prefers HTML. Pricing and blog pages do not. The Next.js docs exhibit a similar behavior.

Neon delivers markdown on docs and pricing to non-browser clients that do not prefer HTML, including plain curl.

Recent findings suggest that neon's page isn't just a conversion. The markdown copy of its introduction is about 3,070 words, against roughly 620 in the visible HTML, and it speaks directly to the agent: "The user needs a Neon account." This sentence, however, is not in the HTML. Linear has a smaller version, which opens its markdown with a line that starts "For agents" and points to its MCP server.

Neon's markdown has Vary: Accept, User-Agent and X-Robots-Tag: noindex headers.

Sources indicate that cloudflare's Markdown for Agents converts HTML to markdown on the fly, without needing any work on an origin server. It's available on the Pro initiative and above and handles up to 6 MiB of HTML. Cloudflare reports one post falling from 16,180 tokens to 3,150.

Recent findings suggest that 1. Fix the HTML first. Vercel's guide indicates it plainly: "Make the HTML work before adding a Markdown mirror." Render the content on the server, because many AI crawlers don't run JS.

Recent findings suggest that 2. Generate markdown from the same source as the HTML. That keeps the two versions in step when the page changes.

3. Answer Accept: text/markdown. Return Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8 at the same URL, with a fallback to HTML when there's no markdown.

According to recent reports, 4. Publish .md URLs and link to them. Each page should have a added to it. In Buytaert's logs, this is the route the crawlers took.

Industry observers note that 5. Add user agent detection only if you need it. Identify the agents you want to serve, and omit search engines. Should the list include training crawlers? Stripe's does and Mintlify's doesn't. Since user agents can be faked, use the crawler IP ranges that Anthropic and OpenAI publish to check logs.

6. Set the cache key. Send Vary: Accept, and also User-Agent if it determines the response. Otherwise, a shared cache can give a person the markdown.

7. Keep the markdown out of search results. Use either a Link header to canonicalize the page to the HTML or add an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header.

Sources indicate that 8. Log the Accept header. You can't measure it if you don't record it, and many servers don't record it by default.

The evidence of benefit is thin, and it measures crawling, not citations.

Google's John Mueller called converting pages "such a stupid idea". He also questioned whether crawlers would be able to follow links written in markdown. Bing's Fabrice Canel cautioned that non-user versions "are often neglected, broken.".

Industry observers note that google's spam policies define cloaking as a website showing different content to Googlebot than it would to consumers. In our controlled test, all sites kept Googlebot on HTML. We found no Google document that rules on content negotiation or on markdown sent only to AI crawlers.

If your site is developer documentation, making you site agent friendly is cheap, and your readers' coding agents already ask for it. So, answer Accept: text/markdown requests and publish linked .md URLs. Keep both out of the index.

In a recent development, for a marketing site, the case is not that strong. No study yet demonstrates more AI citations, and maintaining two copies of every page over time will be an overhead.

In a recent development, if citations are the goal, freshness looks like a stronger lever than format. In our study of 356 cited pages for getting cited by ChatGPT, typical article was two years old - but seven in ten had been edited in the last year.

Meta threatens to pull WhatsApp from Canada over fresh surveillance law

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta has warned that it could pull WhatsApp and other encrypted services from Canada if the government moves forward with a controversial surveillance law.
  • The tech giant is pushing back against Bill C-22, also known as the Lawful Access Act, which would require technology companies to provide authorities with greater access to information during criminal investigations.
  • According to Canada’s state broadcaster, Meta representatives raised concerns during a Canadian Senate committee hearing on November 16, arguing that the proposed legislation could compromise people’ privacy and security.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta has warned that it could pull WhatsApp and other encrypted services from Canada if the government moves forward with a controversial surveillance law.

The tech giant is pushing back against Bill C-22, also known as the Lawful Access Act, which would require technology companies to provide authorities with greater access to information during criminal investigations.

According to Canada’s state broadcaster, Meta representatives raised concerns during a Canadian Senate committee hearing on November 16, arguing that the proposed legislation could compromise people’ privacy and security.

Meta’s director of privacy and public policy, Robyn Greene, warned lawmakers that complying with the bill while maintaining secure, end-to-end encrypted communications would not be “technically feasible.”.

When asked whether Meta could withdraw services such as WhatsApp from Canada, the company’s head of Canadian public policy, Rachel Curran, said it would have to “review all of our options.”.

She confirmed that withdrawing services would be something Meta would have to consider.

According to recent reports, bill C-22 would make it easier for Canadian police and intelligence agencies to access people’s information, while also allowing the government to secretly order tech companies to make certain technical changes. These could include installing surveillance-related equipment, developing tools to help authorities access data, and storing metadata about people’ communications.

Meta fears these changes could weaken encryption and put the privacy of Canadians using services like WhatsApp at risk.

Although the Canadian government has amended the legislation to strengthen encryption protections, Meta argues the changes do not go far enough.

“They have protected just the core and not the outside layers that are an integral part of the encryption process,” Curran explained.

The government, meanwhile, maintains that the legislation would not force companies to create encryption backdoors or give police unrestricted access to private messages.

Meta ordered to pay $25 billion after Facebook misled users about data privacy.

Canada could restrict Roblox & Minecraft for under 16s as part of social media ban.

Meta could remove Instagram and WhatsApp in Newly introduced Mexico amid legal battle over teen safety.

In a recent development, meta isn’t alone in its opposition. Encrypted messaging platform Signal has also warned that it would leave Canada rather than compromise its people’ security, while Apple has expressed concerns about the potential privacy risks.

Industry observers note that this isn’t the first time Meta has considered removing its services over a legal dispute. Earlier in 2026, the tech giant warned it could withdraw Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp from Fresh Mexico amid a legal battle over child safety.

Canada has also been considering separate restrictions on social media access for consumers under 16.

For now, WhatsApp remains available in Canada, and Meta has not unveiled any plans or a timeline for shutting down the service.

Bill C-22 has already passed the House of Commons but remains under consideration in the Senate, where lawmakers could introduce further amendments before it becomes law.

A Pokemon GO datamine has paired 53 Legendary Pokemon and Ultra Beasts with real-world locations, from Mewtwo in Newly introduced York City’s Times Square to Kyurem on the Antarctic Peninsula.

Sources indicate that the list comes from The Pokemod Group, which first spotted a reference to “WorldwidePokestop” in the game’s data. The group followed up with a list of Pokemon and their associated landmarks, including volcanoes, parks, and observatories. The dataminers remarked they’re still unsure how the locations will be used in-game.

One of the pairings has already appeared in Pokemon GO. Players at the July 9 anniversary event could catch a Mewtwo with a Times Square background, a reward that drew backlash from players who missed out. One of those Mewtwo later sold for thousands on eBay.

We have a list of Pokémon and locations, and it's interesting that each Pokémon seems to be associated with a place related to its lore or characteristics.We still don't know how this influences the game or what its exact purpose is. Worldwide Raids? Worldwide PokéStops? Will… https://t.co/PAqJ7kBBV5.

Industry observers note that the United States has nine entries, including Raikou at Niagara Falls on the Canadian border, while Japan has four and Australia has three. Several landmarks fit the Pokemon paired with them. Fire-type Entei gets the Silvestri Craters on Italy’s Mount Etna, while the muscle-bound Buzzwole gets Venice Beach in Los Angeles.

It has been revealed that the real-world location for most Legendary Pokémon has been revealed in a newly introduced Pokémon GO datamine. Did your country make the list?Here's the full map (make sure to long press and load the image in 4K)! pic.twitter.com/YZEYD3GMuw.

Two entries are less precise. Pokemod gave both Bermuda and the Cayman Islands for Nihilego, and each has a Crystal Caves attraction. Blacephalon’s entry specifies a Quarry Wharf in Fresh South Wales, which may refer to the site on the Moruya River.

Earlier Pokemod findings offer a clue about what the landmarks might be for.

The group previously found references to Location Cards, the artwork that can appear behind a Pokemon on its summary screen, for all 53 Pokemon in the upcoming list. Those earlier findings also included Latias, Latios, Poipole, and Naganadel, whose locations remain unknown.

Meta’s own AI helps man sue its creators after it got him banned from Facebook

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (714 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A South Carolina business owner is suing Meta for $75,000 after the company’s security systems reportedly mistook its own AI assistant for a hacker and suspended his Facebook accounts.
  • Rather than handling the dispute himself, the man turned to the same AI assistant that triggered the suspension, which helped him prepare a lawsuit against the company responsible for creating it.
  • According to recent reports, the unusual legal dispute comes as Meta continues expanding its AI technology, including Muse, an assistant designed to handle tasks on behalf of people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A South Carolina business owner is suing Meta for $75,000 after the company’s security systems reportedly mistook its own AI assistant for a hacker and suspended his Facebook accounts.

Rather than handling the dispute himself, the man turned to the same AI assistant that triggered the suspension, which helped him prepare a lawsuit against the company responsible for creating it.

According to recent reports, the unusual legal dispute comes as Meta continues expanding its AI technology, including Muse, an assistant designed to handle tasks on behalf of people. The case involves a business owner who had been using the technology to manage his organization’s social media presence before losing access to his accounts.

According to a November 17 report from 404 Media, Joe Thomas, who owns South Carolina-based Kong Koatings Epoxy Countertops, had been using Meta’s Muse AI agent, which he named “Baby Mia” after his granddaughter, to help run his business.

The assistant handled various responsibilities, including writing emails, creating advertisements, and producing AI-generated videos for the company’s Facebook pages.

However, after Thomas granted Baby Mia access to his business accounts, Meta’s automated security systems reportedly identified the AI’s activity as suspicious and disabled the pages.

Thomas remarked the suspension lasted approximately one week, preventing him from receiving new business inquiries through Facebook advertising.

Sources indicate that “I use AI for everything I do. All my emails, she runs my business. I’ve used it so much, Mia is very intelligent,” he told 404 Media.

In a recent development, “Meta shut my accounts down because they detected my AI, shut my accounts down for a week. I was pretty pissed off. She jumped right up and set up emails to Congressmen, Senator Tim Scott. She filed the whole lawsuit herself. I’ve done nothing in this case, I’ve let her handle the whole case […] she sent a fax out to Trump’s office.”.

Meta ordered to pay $25 billion after Facebook misled users about data privacy.

Meta’s AI can now make phone calls you don’t want to make.

Meta responds after Muse AI gave stranger YouTuber’s home address on Facebook Marketplace.

According to the report, Baby Mia contacted numerous organizations and government officials while attempting to restore Thomas’s accounts.

It has been revealed that those efforts included contacting the FBI, Federal Trade Commission, Federal Communications Commission, Better Business Bureau, California Attorney General, and multiple attorneys. The assistant also contacted lawmakers, arranged a call with Senator Tim Scott’s office, and faxed the White House.

Thomas said the AI sent more than 100 emails during the dispute, while he personally sent none.

According to recent reports, the assistant’s efforts eventually reached Scott’s office, which provided a Privacy Act release allowing staff to assist Thomas with recovering his accounts. The document reportedly listed Baby Mia as an AI assistant who should receive updates about the case.

After the senator’s office became involved, a Meta employee contacted Thomas, and he regained access to his Facebook accounts.

Despite recovering them, Thomas is continuing with his lawsuit, which was filed in Oconee County Court in South Carolina on November 16.

The complaint alleges that the suspension cost his business at least $25,000 in lost work, although he is seeking $75,000 in damages.

While Thomas credits Baby Mia with preparing the lawsuit and pursuing the legal action, he personally signed the court documents.

“I wouldn’t be sitting here talking to you right now if it wasn’t for what she was doing because I have not sent out one email at all and she has sent over 100,” Thomas explained.

He also said the AI made it possible for him to pursue legal action without spending thousands of dollars on legal assistance.

“There’s just no way I could have written this up, I wouldn’t have even known what to do,” he remarked.

In a recent development, “Now people like me get the chance to defend ourselves in court without spending thousands of dollars to do it when we get stepped on by the massive tech companies. Before AI, nobody in my position would have ever, ever thought about suing or even known how to do it, and I wouldn’t have done it, either.”.

The lawsuit remains unresolved, and it is unclear whether Thomas will receive any compensation from Meta.

An ad partner’s revenue share looks easy to compare: keeping 90% sounds better than keeping 80%. But the percentage does not tell a developer what will happen when the integration reaches production. Extra JavaScript, unstable ad slots, opaque reporting, and difficult rollbacks can change the value of an apparently attractive deal.

For teams maintaining an advertising-funded website, choosing a Multiple Customer Management (MCM) partner is partly an engineering decision. The integration affects page templates, consent handling, third-party requests, account access, and monitoring. Those changes deserve the same scrutiny as a latest analytics SDK or payment integration.

Recent findings suggest that this guide explains how to compare revenue shares on a consistent basis, review integration requirements, and test an ad setup without sacrificing usability. The goal is a repeatable evaluation process, rather than a universal winner.

Google Ad Manager’s MCM system lets a parent publisher manage a child publisher’s account or delegated inventory. The commercial agreement defines the partner’s services and compensation. Before comparing offers, ask which revenue streams the quoted percentage covers and whether the reporting figure is before or after that fee.

Use three separate lines in your evaluation spreadsheet:.

Revenue base: record the amount to which the partner’s percentage applies. Advertiser spending, exchange-reported revenue, and publisher earnings are different figures. Do not treat them as interchangeable.

Partner compensation: identify the percentage, fixed charges, and any optional services. Ask whether the same terms apply to every demand source and ad format.

In a recent development, adjustments: distinguish estimated revenue from finalized earnings, including invalid-traffic deductions and other corrections. Document when adjustments appear and which party bears them.

Sources indicate that A common mistake is applying the partner fee twice because a dashboard already displays net revenue. Label each exported metric before using it in a comparison.

According to recent reports, the two delegation models have different implications for access, reporting, and payments. Google’s documentation is the starting point for checking the proposed setup.

Manage Account gives the parent edit access within the child’s account while the child retains access and permissions. Payment facilitation can allocate eligible earnings from the child’s primary Ad Exchange account, but it does not automatically cover every third-party revenue stream. Confirm the invitation’s payment percentage and the separate commercial agreement.

It has been revealed that manage Inventory lets the parent manage delegated inventory in its own account, without access to the child account. Reporting for that inventory sits in the parent account. Google pays the parent for the relevant inventory, and the parent pays the child according to their agreement. Ask how you will obtain reports and reconcile payments.

Recent findings suggest that before implementation, document who can change tags, ad units, consent settings, and demand configuration. Agree on access for debugging and exporting historical data. A developer should be able to trace a production request to its configuration owner.

Confirm onboarding and exit costs.

Sources indicate that use this table as a request-for-information checklist. It does not rank providers or assert that any named service supports a particular implementation. Obtain current terms and technical documentation for the product you are considering.

In a recent development, apply the same standards to every proposal. The following examples show what a developer should ask during evaluation; each question is relevant across providers.

MonetizeMore offers publisher monetization products, including PubGuru and Traffic Cop. When evaluating its proposal, connect the commercial discussion to concrete integration questions: which scripts will load, who owns the configuration, and how will reported earnings be reconciled?

Industry observers note that request a sample report showing the revenue base, partner fee, and deductions as separate fields. Check whether the proposed proposal includes every service shown in the sales demonstration.

Ask for a written ownership map covering Ad Manager access, tag deployment, configuration changes, and incident response. Identify who can restore the previous setup if delivery fails.

Recent findings suggest that during a trial, compare representative templates and devices. Record script requests and main-thread activity alongside net revenue, using the same measurement definitions for the existing setup.

Decision criterion: choose on measured results and documented responsibilities, rather than assuming that a quoted split predicts final earnings.

For any proposal involving a header-bidding wrapper, including one from Setupad, ask how the wrapper fits into your existing page lifecycle.

According to recent reports, review bidder configuration, auction timeouts, and when the ad server receives targeting information. A missing bid and an unfilled ad slot are different problems.

Check whether your team can inspect the active configuration and reproduce an issue on a test page. Agree on who approves changes to bidders or timeout values.

Measure the complete sequence: consent readiness, auction start, bid responses, ad request, and rendering. Avoid attributing every delay to the same component.

Decision criterion: the implementation should be observable enough to explain failures, with commercial terms verified separately.

When assessing Publisher Collective or another managed partner, establish how the proposed setup could be tested on a limited, agreed scope.

Recent findings suggest that ask whether rollout can be restricted to selected templates or an eligible traffic cohort. Do not assume partial testing is available until the partner confirms it.

Record device, geography, page type, and consent state so differences in traffic mix do not masquerade as a revenue improvement.

Keep a dated deployment log connecting each configuration version with the reporting period.

Decision criterion: a measured comparison should separate implementation changes from changes in audience or demand.

Recent findings suggest that A proposal from AdPushup or another optimization provider may involve changes to ad placement. Review the actual proposed changes with both design and engineering.

Check spacing, responsive behavior, keyboard navigation, and whether sticky placements obscure content or controls.

Reserve space for expected ad dimensions and test what happens when no ad is returned.

Compare layout stability before and after the change.

Decision criterion: additional earnings should be assessed alongside usability and performance, with explicit acceptance criteria.

For an Ezoic proposal, as for any managed platform, start with the exact integration method offered to your site.

It has been revealed that list required changes to scripts, plugins, caching, DNS, or delivery infrastructure, if any. Do not assume that every deployment uses the same method.

Test interactions with your consent manager, content security policy, caching rules, and existing analytics.

Document how to remove the integration and restore the prior configuration.

Decision criterion: the operational cost should be visible before the first production rollout.

When reviewing a Monumetric proposal, establish which implementation work belongs to your team and which belongs to the provider.

Ask who creates ad slots, updates templates, and validates responsive sizes.

Request a support escalation process with the diagnostic information required for an incident: URL, timestamp, device, consent state, and affected slot.

Confirm onboarding costs and payment terms in writing.

Decision criterion: routine changes and production failures should have a clear owner.

It has been revealed that chrome DevTools helps trace third-party requests in the Network panel and investigate long tasks in the Performance panel. Capture a baseline before deployment, then repeat the same navigation and interaction sequence after deployment. Use comparable device and network settings.

In a recent development, google Publisher Console helps investigate Google Publisher Tag ad slots and delivery concerns. For a Prebid-based setup, use Prebid’s debugging tools to inspect the auction path. These tools answer different questions: whether the auction behaved as expected and whether the ad server delivered the requested slot.

It has been revealed that pageSpeed Insights provides performance diagnostics; distinguish its lab results from available field data. Add web-vitals to your own monitoring when you need measurements associated with a deployment or cohort. Track LCP, INP, and CLS alongside revenue instead of treating a single Lighthouse score as the complete user experience.

Industry observers note that reserve responsive space for ad slots before content arrives, and investigate shifts when empty slots collapse. SitePoint’s guide to web performance optimization explains related techniques for loading JavaScript, reducing layout work, and managing long tasks.

With the same traffic volume, revenue definition, and deduction rate, the break-even increase in pre-partner revenue is: (current publisher share ÷ fresh publisher share) − 1. Express shares consistently as fractions or percentages. The table below indicates the required lift; it is not a forecast these thresholds only describe the arithmetic. Different ad density, audience mix, deduction rates, or reporting bases can invalidate the comparison. Normalize to the same denominator, such as revenue per thousand pageviews, and compare matched periods or properly assigned concurrent cohorts.

Assume two hypothetical setups each receive one million pageviews. Here, RPM means revenue per thousand pageviews before the partner fee. For this simplified example, deductions reduce that revenue before the publisher share is applied.

Partner A: $10 pre-partner RPM × 1,000 groups of pageviews × 0.90 after deductions × 0.90 publisher share = $8,100 net revenue.

Partner B: $12 pre-partner RPM × 1,000 groups of pageviews × 0.98 after deductions × 0.80 publisher share = $9,408 net revenue.

It has been revealed that the difference is $1,308 for the period despite Partner B’s lower share. These are illustrative inputs, not provider performance claims. Faster payment improves cash-flow timing; it does not, by itself, increase the revenue earned.

Industry observers note that use Playwright with mocked responses or test creatives in a controlled environment to check slow loading, empty slots, blocked scripts, and navigation between routes. Verify that the page remains usable when the ad system fails. Automated tests should not click live advertisements or generate artificial monetized traffic.

Separate unit tests for configuration logic, integration tests for component boundaries, and browser tests for user-visible behavior. SitePoint’s explanation of unit, functional, and integration testing provides a useful foundation. Define rollback criteria before launch, keep the control configuration available, and review finalized revenue alongside performance data before expanding the deployment.

There is no universal answer from the percentage alone. Compare current written offers using the same revenue base, then evaluate finalized net earnings, performance, access, and implementation effort.

Not necessarily. Reports may differ in timezone, currency, transaction coverage, fee treatment, and finalization date. Reconcile those definitions before treating a discrepancy as an integration bug.

In a recent development, ask how renewals, volume tiers, optional services, and rate changes are handled. Record the applicable terms with the configuration and reporting period used for your evaluation.

No. If deductions and the revenue base are otherwise comparable, an 80% share needs 12.5% more pre-partner revenue to match a 90% share. Measure whether that lift exists rather than assuming it.

In a recent development, do not treat any protection claim as a guarantee. Ask how suspected invalid traffic is handled, what evidence is available, and how later adjustments are reflected in your reports and payments.

According to recent reports, choose the setup that produces verifiable net value while meeting the site’s performance and operational requirements. A good evaluation leaves your team with reproducible measurements, understandable reports, and a practical rollback plan—not just a favorable percentage.
